item_title: 118,000 propagules later, the nursery season closes
item_introduction: Three coastal cooperatives beat their first-season target, with 94% of seedlings reaching transplant size.

add_image.image_alt: Mangrove nursery beds beside an estuary channel
add_image.image_caption: Nursery beds at the Sundarbans partner site, near the end of the propagation season.

add_paragraph: The first full season with the three community cooperatives closed this month. Together the nurseries raised **118,000 propagules** of *Rhizophora mucronata* and *Avicennia marina*, and 94% reached transplant size — above the 90% target set at the start of the pilot.

Each cooperative now keeps its own sowing calendar, salinity log and transplant records. The lab supplies seed material, training and a shared quality checklist; day-to-day decisions stay with the nursery teams, which is the point.

Next season adds a second experimental block to test whether a short, controlled salinity shock before transplant improves survival on the mudflat. The results will feed into the blue-carbon accounting workstream and the next open data release.
